# mnemo-jvm-warden
> Application-driven JVM memory vertical right-sizing for Kubernetes without restarts.

## Core Architecture & Problem Alignment
Standard Kubernetes autoscalers are JVM-blind, leading to over-provisioning or reactive OOMKills. Warden orchestrates an inside-out, asymmetric resource coordination layer by communicating directly with the running JVM before executing in-place pod resizes.

- **Target Scenarios:** Minimum-replica HA baselines, slow-booting monoliths, and stateful nodes/distributed caches.
- **Safety Handshake (Asymmetric Scaling):**
  - *SHRINK Loop:* Lower JVM SoftMaxHeapSize/cache -> Force deep GC -> Verify actual RSS < target limit -> Execute Kubernetes in-place resize DOWN.
  - *GROW Loop:* Execute Kubernetes in-place resize UP -> Wait for cgroup headroom -> Raise JVM SoftMaxHeapSize -> Optional cache pre-warming.

## Key Features & Component Topology
- **Warden Controller:** Cluster-wide controller managing `WardenPolicy` and `WardenBoost` CRDs.
- **Warden Agent:** Library sidecar (`shareProcessNamespace: true`) accessing target JVM via JMX/jcmd and host-cgroup mount.
- **Supported GCs:** ZGC and Shenandoah (runtime `SoftMaxHeapSize` adjustments); G1 (scheduled periodic uncommits).
- **Requirements:** Kubernetes 1.35+ (Native In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling GA) and Cluster Autoscaler.

## Custom Resource Definitions (CRD) Reference
*(Note: Full YAML schemas for `WardenPolicy` and `WardenBoost` can be structured in your repository or standard documentation files).*

- **WardenPolicy:** Defines cron-like schedules (`off-peak`, `peak`, and on-demand `boosts`) for shifting memory profiles.
- **WardenBoost (Experimental):** An on-demand, application-driven claim system to temporarily grant memory headroom for isolated heavy operational tasks (e.g., index rebuilds, migrations).

## Security & RBAC Guardrails
- Agent requires `shareProcessNamespace: true` and host cgroup mount to monitor physical RSS.
- For `WardenBoost`, the agent sidecar requires `patch` permissions on its own Pod metadata to write the `warden.mnemo.io/resize-ack` annotation. Harden token visibility to prevent compromise by the primary app container.

## Guides & Articles
- [How to shrink JVM memory in Kubernetes without a restart](https://github.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/blob/main/docs/shrink-jvm-memory-kubernetes.md): why JVM pods get OOMKilled after in-place resize, how to size the smallest memory limit, and why VPA alone is not enough.
- [Your JVMs Are Burning Money Overnight](https://baokhang.hashnode.dev/shrink-jvm-memory-kubernetes-in-place-resize): hands-on walkthrough with a three-replica Spring Boot demo.
- [Java lease client (warden-boost-client on Maven Central)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.baokhang83.mnemo/warden-boost-client)
